title: mos.tray.v1
description: Outcome of a tray-control verb emitted by `mos tray <action> --json`: the first commands mos issues that CHANGE drive state (eject/close via START STOP UNIT 0x1B, lock/unlock via PREVENT ALLOW MEDIUM REMOVAL 0x1E). Mechanism facts only — mos reports what the command did and does NOT unmount for you (the deliberate contrast with `drutil tray eject`'s policy). A command the drive ANSWERED is success (the process exits 0) even when the outcome is a refusal; a transport/lock failure (drive mounted or held by another client, gone, IO) emits mos.error.v1 and a non-zero exit instead. Design: doc/research/2026-06-13-tray-control-feasibility.md; encoding: T10 04-349r1.

bsd_node.description: Whole-disk dev node of the current media, or null when the drive is empty (an eject of an empty tray is still a valid command).

registry_id.description: Drive service IORegistry entry ID — attachment identity. 0 = unavailable. NOT durable: replug mints a new ID.

action.description: The control verb issued. eject/close are START STOP UNIT (LoEj=1, START=0/1); lock/unlock are PREVENT ALLOW MEDIUM REMOVAL.

force.description: eject only (null on every other action): true when --force was requested — "open no matter what". The eject is attempted and, on a clearable blocker, the blocker is cleared and the eject re-issued: a Finder/system mount is FORCE-UNMOUNTED (DADiskUnmount, data-loss capable — kills open file handles), and a basic Prevent lock is cleared (along with the persistent state, so a lock in the way leaves nothing locked). The one blocker --force cannot clear is another userland client holding exclusive access (no SCSI preempt): that surfaces as mos.error.v1 with code exclusive_access. Without --force a mounted disc is mos.error.v1 busy and a basic lock is outcome refused_locked — both reported facts, nothing cleared.

persistent.description: lock/unlock only (null on every other action): selects the PERSISTENT bit (04-349r1 Table 8). lock true sets the Persistent Prevent state (byte4 0x03 — the robot-grade lock: operator eject button becomes a GESN EjectRequest event); false sets the basic Prevent state (0x01). unlock must match the lock being released — the two prevent states are independent (0x00 clears basic, 0x02 clears persistent).

outcome.description: done = command completed GOOD. refused_locked = CHECK CONDITION 5/53/02 MEDIA REMOVAL PREVENTED (an eject/close hit a basic Prevent lock — a reported fact, not a CLI failure). refused_other = any other answered CHECK CONDITION (e.g. a drive without Persistent Prevent support rejecting --persistent with 5/24/00).

sense.description: SCSI sense triple the drive returned on a refusal, or null. Populated for any answered refusal — refused_locked is always 5/53/02; refused_other carries whatever the drive reported (e.g. 5/24/00 INVALID FIELD IN CDB for a drive without Persistent Prevent support), so a consumer can diagnose a non-lock refusal. Always null on done.

allOf.title: force is a boolean only for eject
persistent is a boolean only for lock/unlock
